mechanism: When recent volatility is high, transformer temperature is in a transient-dominated regime, so historical segments with similarly high recent volatility are more predictive.
failure_condition: low or moderate recent volatility; stable thermal periods
retrieval_action: Upweight historical windows whose recent_volatility was high.
reason: High recent volatility indicates active load or ambient changes; future short-term fluctuations depend on those transient dynamics.
expected_effect: Matches transient thermal response and avoids averaging across stable and turbulent regimes.

mechanism: When recent slope is nearly flat at night, transformer cooling dominates and the future trajectory tends to follow the typical nighttime decay.
activation_condition: when recent_slope_magnitude is low AND hour_of_day is night
failure_condition: day hours or high recent slope magnitude
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to nighttime hours and prefer historical windows with low recent slope magnitude.
reason: At night load and ambient temperature are typically lower, so temperature moves toward equilibrium; same-hour night history is more relevant.
expected_effect: Captures nighttime cooling behavior instead of daytime load and ambient ramps.

mechanism: When the transformer is already at high temperature in summer, future temperature behavior is more sensitive to cooling limitations and should be inferred from hot summer days.
activation_condition: when seasonal_level is summer AND recent_level is high
failure_condition: cool seasons or low recent level
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to summer history and prefer windows with high recent level.
reason: High ambient and high oil temperature alter cooling rates and overload risk, making hot summer segments more representative.
expected_effect: Matches seasonal ambient conditions and high thermal state, reducing bias from cooler-season dynamics.

mechanism: On workdays with strong recent slope, industrial and commercial load ramps dominate, so same workday ramp history is more predictive.
activation_condition: when working_day is workday AND recent_slope_magnitude is high
failure_condition: non-working days or low recent slope magnitude
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to workdays and prefer historical windows with high recent slope magnitude.
reason: Workday load schedules drive strong temperature rises; weekend history is misleading during such ramps.
expected_effect: Matches weekday load ramp timing and amplitude, improving forecasts during active work periods.

mechanism: On non-working days with low volatility, transformer load is typically lower and smoother, so future behavior resembles past stable non-working-day periods.
activation_condition: when working_day is non_working AND recent_volatility is low
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to non-working days and prefer windows with low recent volatility.
reason: Non-working days have distinct load profiles; low volatility indicates a stable non-working regime.
expected_effect: Uses weekend-specific lower-load dynamics and avoids workday load patterns.

mechanism: High recent autocorrelation indicates strong thermal inertia and persistent forcing, so future temperature is best inferred from past segments with similarly high autocorrelation.
failure_condition: low recent autocorrelation or rapid regime changes
retrieval_action: Prefer historical windows with high recent autocorrelation.
reason: High autocorrelation means the current temperature state dominates near-future behavior; similar highly persistent segments share this inertia.
expected_effect: Matches persistent thermal dynamics and yields smoother, more accurate short-term continuation.

mechanism: During evening hours, transformer temperature often peaks due to residual load and ambient cooling lag, so same-evening history is more predictive.
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to evening hours to capture late-day thermal peak and decay.
reason: The evening transition combines high residual heat and falling ambient temperature, creating a distinct daily segment.
expected_effect: Matches diurnal phase and reduces mixing of morning rise and afternoon peak patterns.

mechanism: In transitional seasons, moderate ambient and load conditions make historical segments from the same season more predictive than summer or winter extremes.
activation_condition: when seasonal_level is autumn OR spring
retrieval_action: Prefer same-season historical windows, matching the current transitional season.
reason: Transitional seasons have distinct cooling behavior and load patterns; same-season history is more relevant.
expected_effect: Improves forecast representativeness by avoiding summer and winter extremes during moderate seasons.
